points.description: States that a class definition includes data members (attributes/variables/fields) AND member functions (methods).
points.partial_credit: Half-credit (2 marks) if only one of data members or member functions is given, or both are named vaguely or with a minor error.

points.description: Both components are named distinctly as two separate things: data members (attributes) for the state, and member functions for the behaviour/operations.
points.partial_credit: Half-credit if both are mentioned but not clearly distinguished as two separate kinds of members.

rubric.notes: Full marks for saying a class contains data members (attributes/variables) and member functions (methods), in any wording. Part marks if only one of the two is given or the wording is vague. Give no marks for unrelated answers, such as only access specifiers or only objects, that mention neither data members nor member functions. Extra correct detail, such as constructors or access specifiers, is fine.
